description:
Signed-off-by: NAYANAR <nayana.r7813@gmail.com>
#1365 

Files Modified
1. Backend - admin.py

Added tag_search query parameter to 5 partial endpoints:

/admin/servers/partial - Virtual Servers
/admin/tools/partial - Tools
/admin/prompts/partial - Prompts
/admin/resources/partial - Resources
/admin/a2a/partial - A2A Agents
Each endpoint filters across multiple database fields:

name, description, tags, owner_email
Plus entity-specific fields (e.g., url for tools, uri for resources)
2. Frontend - admin.js

Added performServerSideSearch() - triggers HTMX request with tag_search parameter
Added debouncedServerSearch() - 300ms debounce to avoid excessive requests
Updated clearSearch() - reloads data without filter
3. Templates - admin.html

Added oninput="debouncedServerSearch('entityType', this.value)" to all search inputs for reliable event handling
How It Works
User types in search box
After 300ms debounce, JavaScript sends HTMX GET request with ?tag_search=term&page=1
Server filters ALL records in database using SQL LIKE queries
Returns first page of matching results
Pagination automatically preserves the search term

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body: This function is identical to the one on `admin.py`. They can be merged in a `utils.py` file and import with both.

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body:
`tag_search` seems like a search for tags. The `searchTerm` used in `admin.js` might be clearer, would you consider renaming this to `search_term`?

Also, as it's a user input variable, I recommend adding a length limit to it.

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body: As the search term is lowered (line 498), I recommend either lowering the field as done on the else condition (removing the need for if altogether), or not lowering the search term when escaping it, an then lowering both the pattern and the field on the else clause.

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body: This refactor is really neat, good job!

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body:
The user input is being printed directly into log messages at INFO level. This has two issues:
 - Log injection risk: Crafted search terms with newlines or log format characters can corrupt log output or confuse log parsers.
 - Noise: Logging every search keystroke at INFO level in production (debounced at 300ms, but still high-frequency) will flood logs. Should be DEBUG at most.

Recommendation: Change to LOGGER.debug(...) and sanitise the search term (strip newlines and truncate to reasonable length)
